diagnosis.title: Charging voltage too high
diagnosis.meaning: The regulator is not limiting the alternator. Sustained over-voltage boils and swells AGM batteries and can damage lights and electronics.

causes.cause: Regulator sense or earth connection poor

fix: Avoid long rides until fixed; switch off unneeded loads.
Check the regulator/rectifier connectors and earth under the headlight.
Test the regulator/rectifier (manual p.712–713) and replace if it fails.

parts.where: At the front, on the fork below the headlight (lower yoke area).
parts.access: Visible from the front under the headlight.

diagnosis.title: Fault code P0605: Engine control module
diagnosis.meaning: The ECM has confirmed this fault and lit the warning lamp.

causes.cause: Connector or wiring for engine control module

fix: Look the code up in the service manual DTC table (p.301–306) to confirm Triumph’s meaning.
Follow the pinpoint test for this system (manual p.289).
Check the connector for this part first: most intermittent codes are connections.
Clear the code only after the fix, then confirm it stays clear on a test ride. Adaption cannot run while an engine code is present (TB 168.2).
